title: ephemeral-fallback-limiter-and-priority-calibrator
author: Ava Patel
description: Motivation: During a recent regional overload incident we observed rapid oscillation between failover and reopen states for a subset of tenants when KV pressure and short-lived traffic spikes coincided. This caused noisy fallbacks and unnecessary cross-region egress. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms to make degradation behavior more stable and predictable: 1) an Ephemeral Fallback Limiter (EFL) that rate-limits transient fallback decisions using a lease-backed admission window, with hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping; 2) a Priority Calibrator that adjusts tenant evict/holdoff weights based on recent SLO burn and tokenized latency percentiles to preserve fairness across cohorts. Key design points: EFL uses a lightweight distributed lease (existing ring-based lease store) so decisions survive restarts but expire quickly; limiter accepts short bursts but enforces a decaying allowance when repeated fallbacks occur; Priority Calibrator runs per-routing cohort and translates observed P95/P99 latency deltas into small, timeboxed weight nudges rather than large immediate reassignments. Scope: runtime admission controller, a new calibration controller in controlplane, observability additions (metrics and traces), config knobs in console defaults, and a small compatibility shim so Dedicated pools with older agents fall back to a safe default. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-3621) - [x] unit tests for limiter logic - [x] integration test with simulated KV pressure - [x] e2e canary rollout (10% traffic) - [x] console flag and README snippet - [x] telemetry dashboards updated - [x] feature gated behind runtime flag for safe rollback Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary clusters for 48h, monitor SLO burn, P99 tail latency, cross-region egress. If SLO burn increases >10% relative to baseline revert flag. Backwards compatibility: if controlplane calibration fails or RPC times out, runtime falls back to a stable-weight method; Dedicated agents without lease support use a local in-memory limiter with stricter thresholds. Why different from previous approaches: this implementation explicitly ties short-term fallback allowances to a rapidly expiring lease and couples it to observed SLO deltas to avoid permanent demotions for transient noise. Commits summary: - add ephemeral fallback limiter core + unit tests - implement priority calibrator controller + integration tests - add metrics/traces and console feature flag - compatibility shim for old dedicated agents - update docs and rollout script Changed files (high-level): - runtime/admission/efl_limiter.go - controlplane/calibrator/controller.go - controlplane/calibrator/calibrator_test.go - observability/metrics/efl_metrics.md - console/feature_flags.yaml - ci/canary-rollout/efl_rollout.sh - tests/integration/kv_pressure_simulator.go - docs/runbooks/ephemeral-fallback.md - charts/dedicated/compat-shim.yaml Impacted areas: runtime admission path (hot), controlplane calibration loop (medium), console defaults (low), Dedicated agent compatibility handling (small).
